target.name: NetworkOcean
target.founder: Sam Mendel (CEO; serial founder, prior exit of a creator-hiring marketplace), Eric Kim (CTO; ex-Palantir, Merge; Cornell)

methods.name: Stage-Progression
methods.rationale: Applies typical Seed → next-stage step-up multiplier (2.5x) to $1M total raised proxy.

data.narrative:
NetworkOcean is a seed-stage maritime technology company founded by Sam Mendel (prior creator-hiring marketplace exit) and Eric Kim (ex-Palantir, Merge). The company operates in the ocean and maritime sector alongside three identifiable private peers—Standard Subsea, Clippership, and Albacore—with no directly comparable public comparables available.

Valuation was derived using a stage-progression method, the primary applicable triangulation approach given limited market data at the frontier-tech intersection. Using the company's $1M total raised as a base value proxy and applying a 2.5x step-up multiplier typical of seed-to-next-stage financing rounds, the analysis yields an implied post-money valuation of $2.5M. This represents a standard progression for early-stage venture deployment and accounts for founder pedigree (serial founder with exit experience; technical depth from Palantir and infrastructure-scale prior roles).

The triangulated valuation range is $2.1M (low) to $2.9M (median $2.5M, high $3M). This narrow band reflects reliance on a single defensible method; the primary uncertainty stems from limited public and private comparable trading data in the ocean-maritime technology space. Resolution of valuation precision will require either (1) closer comp-based benchmarking as the sector matures, or (2) progression to the next financing round, which would establish market-cleared pricing. Key sensitivities include product-market validation timelines and the pace of capital deployment within the maritime tech vertical.
